They came to a royal wedding, but never made it home.
How did a proposal of love turn into one of the darkest tragedies in the history of the archipelago?
This is the story of the Battle of Bubat.
In 1357, Majapahit is at the peak of its glory under King Hayam Wuruk.
He falls in love with Dyah Pitaloka, the princess of the Sunda Kingdom, and sends her a proposal.
King Linggabuana of Sunda agrees, and sets off for Majapahit with his family and a small escort.
No war army, just a wedding party carrying gifts.
They camp at Bubat Field, waiting for the wedding day.
But trouble comes from Gajah Mada, the prime minister.
He is still obsessed with finishing his Palapa Oath, to unite the whole archipelago under Majapahit.
And Sunda is the kingdom that has never bowed.
So Gajah Mada rejects an equal marriage.
He demands that Dyah Pitaloka be handed over as tribute, a sign that Sunda has surrendered.
Humiliated, King Linggabuana refuses to bow.
Majapahit troops surround Bubat Field.
The Sundanese are hopelessly outnumbered, with only ceremonial guards.
Yet they choose to fight to the last drop of blood.
King Linggabuana falls in battle.
And Dyah Pitaloka chooses to end her own life to protect her honor.
Hayam Wuruk is too late to stop it.
He is heartbroken, and furious.
The bond between Majapahit and Sunda breaks for centuries.
And Gajah Mada is pushed out of his post.
One political ambition turned a celebration of love into a scar on history.
So what finally brought down a kingdom as mighty as Majapahit?
